pages.text: Shrines are multiblock hallows that have been marked by a Practitioner. To designate a multiblock hallow as a shrine, shift-right-click it with an empty hand. This costs a bit of health, but not Self. When a hallow becomes a shrine, its particles start moving over its surface instead of drifting aimlessly. You can add new blocks to a shrine and they will become part of it.

Many shrines can be $(bold)overflowed$() (filled while already full) or $(bold)overdrawn$() (extracted from when empty) to cause effects in a range around the shrine. You can see these ranges in your Sight. The volume of a shrine's range is proportional to its total capacity. Wider shrines will have wider ranges, and taller shrines will have taller ranges.

These overflow/overdraw abilities only trigger if they have enough fuel/capacity to have an effect. For instance, nature shrines can use 33 overflow spirits to grow crops, so they won't break down seeds directly since seeds only have 30 nature spirits. To make this work, you'd need an intermediate nature hallow that can hold at least 33 spirits to be drained all at once.

If you use a spirit tablet on a shrine, every spirit in that shrine will be spent to turn the tablet into a hallow.$(br2)The new hallow will be empty, but its capacity will be equal to the number of spent spirits.$(br2)There is no limit to the potential capacity of these hallows.
